rows.jp: つれづれと、時は流れた。

ghs.en: Hours flowed by in dull tedium.

rows.jp: 残った時間を、俺は読書をして過ごした。
rows.en: I spent what remained of it reading.

ghs.en: I have been spending the remaining time in reading.

rows.jp: 以前は理解できなかったものが、最近は読めることに気づいた。
rows.en: Lately, I had discovered I could read things that once defeated me.

ghs.en: I realized that things that I could not understand before I could now manage to read.

rows.jp: これから俺は、多くの時間を浪費し、わずかなものを得ることになるだろう。
rows.en: From now on, I would squander great stretches of time and come away with very little.

ghs.en: From here onwards I will be wasting a lot of time, and all I will obtain will be tiny little things.

rows.jp: 支払いがほんの一週間、増えただけのことだ。
rows.en: The price had merely gone up by a single week.

ghs.en: This is just an increase in its price, an increase of a mere single week.
I flip back and forth through the pages.

rows.jp: 文字列を脳にインプットしながら、ただ時間を消費した。
rows.en: I passed the time feeding line after line into my brain.

ghs.en: A mere expenditure of time while inputting character strings into the brain.
The Capture, the route, has failed.

rows.jp: 故に、やり直す必要があった。
rows.en: Therefore, I had to start over.

ghs.en: Ergo, it is necessary to do all over again.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that it was therefore necessary to start over. The English changes the tense to present and omits the object after 'do.'
ghs.remedy: it was necessary to do it all over again

highlights.text: it is necessary to do all over again

rows.jp: 便利なリセットは、週末にしかない仕様だ。
rows.en: By design, the convenient reset only came at the end of the week.

ghs.en: The specifications of our convenient reset put it outside of choice at the weekend.
ghs.assessment: The convenient reset is designed to be available only on the weekend. The English says that it is outside the available choices at the weekend, implying the opposite.
ghs.remedy: is only available on the weekend

highlights.text: put it outside of choice at the weekend

rows.jp: またこうした日々は、いずれやってくる楽園での、生きる予習にもなる。
rows.en: Days like these were practice, too—preparing me to live in the paradise that would come someday.

ghs.en: And these days themselves will also become a lesson, a preparation for life in the Eden that will one day come.

rows.jp: 時間をかけて生きる癖をつけないといけない。
rows.en: I had to learn how to live at an unhurried pace.

ghs.en: It is indispensable to grow into the habit, however bad, of living while expending time.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he must get used to taking time to live. The English calls the habit bad and recasts living patiently as expending time.
ghs.remedy: get into the habit of taking time to live

highlights.text: habit, however bad, of living while expending time

rows.en: I happened to glance out the window.

ghs.en: Casually, I look out of the window.

rows.jp: 蝉も鳴かない世界だが、どこかに誰かがいる。
rows.en: No cicadas sang in this world, but somewhere in it, someone was there.

ghs.en: Even in this world where not even the cicadas cry somewhere, someone, must be among us.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese contrasts a world where even cicadas are silent with the fact that somebody exists somewhere. The English misattaches 'somewhere' to the cicadas and produces an ungrammatical claim that somebody must be among the narrator's group.
ghs.remedy: Though not even cicadas sing in this world, somebody is out there somewhere.

highlights.text: where not even the cicadas cry somewhere, someone, must be among us

rows.jp: 感じることはできないが、そういう事実がある。
rows.en: I couldn't sense them, but I knew it for a fact.

ghs.en: That is something I cannot sense, yet, this is the truth:

rows.jp: どこかに誰かがいるということ。
あまりにも健全で、あたたかくて、胸がほんの少しだけ締めつけられたのだった。
rows.en: It was all so wholesome, so warm, that my chest tightened just a little.

ghs.en: so excessively wholesome in its warmth the what is inside the chest tightened, only just a little.
ghs.assessment: The wholesome warmth makes Taichi's chest tighten slightly. The English substitutes an ungrammatical unidentified thing inside the chest.

highlights.text: the what is inside the chest tightened
